title: Improve clinical dengue outcomes with an approved direct-acting antiviral

concept.text: Treat early dengue infection with an antiviral that reduces clinically important illness or progression. Mosnodenvir demonstrated human prophylactic antiviral activity, but that does not establish therapeutic benefit; its phase 2 field-prevention programme was discontinued. Proposed completion test: Regulatory approval following a randomized phase 3 trial in naturally infected patients treated early in illness, showing superiority on a prespecified clinical endpoint such as progression to severe dengue, hospitalization or sustained symptom resolution, with virological outcomes supportive. Test set by: A regulator would decide approval; no universally accepted dengue-antiviral efficacy threshold was identified. The clinical endpoint and early-treatment requirement are proposed editorial criteria. Overlaps: VIR-02. Sources given: [Primary mosnodenvir prophylaxis trial record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41297006/?fc=None&ff=20260215191432&v=2.18.0.post22+67771e2) ; [Sponsor announcement discontinuing the field-prevention study](https://www.jnj.com/media-center/press-releases/johnson-johnson-to-discontinue-phase-2-field-study-evaluating-investigational-antiviral-for-the-prevention-of-dengue).

page.title: FDA-approved direct-acting antiviral treatment for symptomatic dengue
page.definition: A medicine approved by the US Food and Drug Administration to reduce illness in people who already have dengue symptoms. It acts on the virus itself. A small molecule can block viral replication, and a neutralizing monoclonal antibody can bind the virus and prevent it from infecting cells. The leading investigational treatment, SII Dengue mAb, has shown antiviral activity in patients.

goal.need: In 2024, countries reported 14,434,584 dengue cases, including 52,738 severe cases and 11,201 deaths. Fluids, fever relief and monitoring are the mainstays of care. Prompt intensive care can save lives, but it does not stop the virus from multiplying. An effective early treatment could shorten fever and pain and help patients avoid severe illness requiring hospital care. Reaching patients in time matters because viral replication can peak before they seek care.

completion.title: FDA approves a direct-acting antiviral with a clinical treatment benefit in dengue.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing approval through a new drug application for a small molecule or a biologics licence application for an antibody, with an indication for treating symptomatic dengue. The approved prescribing information establishes the clinical treatment benefit and the population in which benefits outweigh risks. The applicable approval requirements for effectiveness, safety, product quality and labeling are satisfied.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration; approval standards described in Benefit-Risk Assessment for New Drug and Biological Products, section II.A.
completion.threshold_quote: must determine that the drug is safe and effective for use under the conditions prescribed, recommended, or suggested in the product’s labeling.
completion.basis: Marketing approval supplies an externally adjudicated test of the treatment claim and its benefit–risk balance. FDA describes this determination as specific to the proposed indication and population. WHO’s treatment profile seeks shorter clinical illness and preferably less progression to severe dengue; an antiviral laboratory signal alone does not establish those benefits.

milestones.criterion: Preclinical pharmacology and toxicology data support the conclusion that the candidate is reasonably safe at the proposed initial exposure in a small human study.

milestones.criterion: Human studies characterize tolerability, adverse effects across the doses tested, and drug exposure over time sufficiently to select doses and design a controlled phase 2 study.

milestones.title: A regulator authorizes a randomized dengue-antiviral treatment trial in infected patients.
milestones.criterion: A national medicines regulator authorizes a protocol that randomly assigns patients with confirmed symptomatic dengue to receive the candidate or placebo as treatment.
milestones.set_by: Anvisa, EYU688 phase 2a authorization notice; this notice concerns a small molecule. Indian regulatory authorization of the antibody protocol is documented in the Dengue-mAb trial report.
milestones.threshold_quote: Aprovação refere-se ao ensaio clínico Fase 2a de medicamento de uso oral, inibidor de replicação dos quatro sorotipos do vírus da dengue.

milestones.title: Infectious virus falls more by 24 hours with dengue treatment than with placebo at two-sided P < 0.05.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized treatment trial, adults aged 18–60 with a positive dengue NS1 antigen test present within 48 hours of fever onset. Among those with measurable infectious virus in blood before dosing, the adjusted mean fall in log10 infectious-virus titre from baseline to 24 hours is greater with treatment than with placebo at two-sided P < 0.05.
milestones.set_by: Serum Institute of India, Dengue-mAb-02 phase 2 protocol and published statistical analysis. The endpoint and significance threshold are specific to this antibody trial.
milestones.threshold_quote: Two-tailed P < .05 was considered statistically significant.

milestones.title: Adding a dengue antiviral to supportive care shortens time to sustained recovery in a phase 3 trial.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized, double-blind phase 3 trial, time to sustained recovery is shorter with treatment than with placebo, with supportive care in both groups. The registered antibody protocol compares a single 6 mg/kg infusion with placebo in patients aged ≥5 years with NS1 antigen- or PCR-confirmed dengue and no warning signs or severe dengue. Infusion starts within 72 hours of symptom onset. Recovery assessments through day 28 include temperature, haematocrit stability, platelet count and absence of warning signs or severe dengue. Visits on days 8–27 are optional if symptoms persist.
milestones.set_by: Drugs for Neglected Diseases initiative, protocol DNDi-DmAb-01-DEN, ISRCTN50970152. This published clinical endpoint is specified for a monoclonal antibody.
milestones.threshold_quote: Demonstrate that Dengue monoclonal antibody compared to placebo reduces the time to sustained recovery from dengue fever

milestones.title: A dengue antiviral shows specific, measurable activity against dengue virus in vitro.
milestones.criterion: Before human testing, the candidate or an active metabolite demonstrates a quantifiable antiviral effect against dengue virus in vitro.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Antiviral Product Development, section III.B.1.
milestones.threshold_quote: the investigational product and/or its metabolites show specific, quantifiable antiviral activity in vitro before initiating tests in humans

milestones.title: FDA accepts a marketing application for symptomatic dengue treatment for substantive review.
milestones.criterion: FDA determines that the new drug application for a small molecule or the biologics license application for an antibody is complete for review and files it for the proposed symptomatic dengue treatment indication.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, MAPP 6025.4, revision 1.
milestones.threshold_quote: If the application is complete for review, the application will be filed.

not_found: No dengue-specific FDA or EMA numerical minimum clinical effect size was found.
ISRCTN50970152 does not publish sustained-recovery cutoffs, a target sample size or a statistical success boundary.
No published phase 3 dengue-treatment efficacy result was found for either modality.
The WHO-hosted treatment-profile PDF was inaccessible; an archived copy of the WHO document was accessible.
Publisher full texts of the VIS513 phase 1 and AT-752 phase 2 papers were inaccessible; their indexed PubMed abstracts were available.

results.finding: VIS513: 40 healthy adults received antibody or placebo in the first-in-human study after preclinical safety and efficacy were confirmed.
results.quote: After confirmation of safety and efficacy in preclinical studies, it was tested in a first-in-human study to assess the safety and pharmacokinetics.

results.finding: VIS513: 40 adults participated; 28 of 34 antibody recipients had treatment-related adverse events.
results.detail: No serious adverse events occurred. Median elimination half-life ranged from 775 to 878 hours; the authors reported dose-proportionate exposure and supported further evaluation in dengue patients.
results.quote: Of these 143 adverse events, 80 were treatment-related adverse events in 28 (82%) of 34 participants.

results.finding: In a phase 1 study of JNJ-1802 (N = 86 healthy adults), terminal elimination half-life was 6.3–9.2 days.
results.detail: The study population consisted of healthy adults. The authors identified confirmation of safety and pharmacokinetics in dengue patients as a limitation.
results.quote: The long terminal elimination half-life of JNJ-1802 (t 1/2term  was 6.3–9.2 days) minimizes the risk of a drop in exposure in case of a missed dose and suggests that exposure persists long after stopping of dosing.

results.finding: Anvisa authorized a phase 2a trial of an oral dengue antiviral. Sample size was unspecified.
results.quote: Aprovação refere-se ao ensaio clínico Fase 2a de medicamento de uso oral, inibidor de replicação dos quatro sorotipos do vírus da dengue.

results.finding: Dengue-mAb phase 2 safety analysis included 249 dosed adults and found zero treatment-related serious adverse events.
results.detail: The phase 2 study collected pharmacokinetic samples from a subset of 15 participants per group.
results.quote: No participants reported causally related SAEs.

results.finding: India’s regulatory authority approved the Dengue-mAb placebo-controlled treatment protocol, under which 250 adults were randomized.
Among 31 adults evaluable at 24 hours, Dengue-mAb 9 mg/kg lowered infectious titre more than placebo (two-sided P = .003).
results.detail: Table 2’s 24-hour row governs the comparison. The primary outcomes paragraph labels the 8-hour estimates as 24-hour results. Fever onset was recalled, and the authors suspected some participants presented outside the window.

results.detail: The trial enrolled adults aged 18–60. The phase 3 protocol includes patients aged ≥5 and assesses recovery through day 28 using temperature, haematocrit, platelets, and absence of warning signs or severe dengue.

results.finding: AT-752 had a minimum 39-fold preclinical safety margin over the first-in-human starting dose. Animal sample sizes were unreported.
results.detail: The authors calculated the margins from body-surface-area-scaled animal doses using a reference human body weight of 60 kg.
results.quote: Based on the body surface area conversion factor of 0.162 in rats and 0.324 in monkeys ( 19 ), the human equivalent doses calculated were 162 and 324 mg/kg/day, respectively, in the two animal species, providing 39- and 77-fold of margin of safety for the human starting dose.

results.finding: AV-1 had a >90-fold preclinical safety margin at the proposed starting dose for the phase 1a trial (planned n=40).
results.detail: The sponsor protocol summarizes the preclinical evidence. The text provides no independent replication or regulatory decision establishing the reported safety margin.
results.quote:
The 
proposed initial starting dose provides a >90-fold safety margin when compared to the human 
equivalent dose NOAEL identified from the nonclinical safety study.

results.finding: The Philippine FDA authorized the AT-752 randomized dengue treatment trial on 2022-02-08, with approximately 60 participants planned overall.
results.detail: Actual Philippine enrollment was unspecified. The registry lists the trial as terminated by sponsor decision.

title = "FDA-approved direct-acting antiviral treatment for symptomatic dengue". Reason: The title omits the jurisdiction and symptomatic treatment indication specified by the completion test.

definition = "A medicine approved by the US Food and Drug Administration to reduce illness in people who already have dengue symptoms. It acts on the virus itself. A small molecule can block viral replication, and a neutralizing monoclonal antibody can bind the virus and prevent it from infecting cells. The leading investigational treatment, SII Dengue mAb, has shown antiviral activity in patients.". Reason: The definition leaves the approving authority implicit and gives readers no point of comparison with the leading investigational treatment.

goal.need = "In 2024, countries reported 14,434,584 dengue cases, including 52,738 severe cases and 11,201 deaths. Fluids, fever relief and monitoring are the mainstays of care. Prompt intensive care can save lives, but it does not stop the virus from multiplying. An effective early treatment could shorten fever and pain and help patients avoid severe illness requiring hospital care. Reaching patients in time matters because viral replication can peak before they seek care.". Reason: The current rationale counts confirmed infections but omits severe illness, deaths, the benefit patients need and the short window for treatment.

add statement by European Commission, 2026: "Developing dengue therapeutics, including direct-acting antivirals, host-directed therapies and monoclonal antibodies". Reason: The European Commission roadmap explicitly identifies direct-acting drugs alongside antibodies in its dengue research priorities.
